ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Transaction Reports Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 3631, as amended through 2024), particularly Articles 3, 4, 5-2 and 18; Act on the Prohibition of Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction (Act No. 10078, as amended); Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Book IV governing Chusik Hoesa stock corporations and shareholder registers; Regulations on Identification of Customers and Verification of Beneficial Owners issued by the Financial Services Commission and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Commercial Registration Court (District Court Registry Office) of the municipal or provincial court where the registered office is located
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for destination countries that are parties to the Hague Apostille Convention; for non-member destination countries, separate consular legalization by the destination country's embassy or consulate in the Republic of Korea is the exclusive alternative path. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must never be applied sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of the Articles of Association
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Commercial Registration Court (District Court Registry Office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for Apostille Convention states; for non-member states, consular legalization through the destination state's embassy or consulate in Seoul is the sole alternative path; Apostille and consular legalization shall not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Active Corporate Status Certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Commercial Registration Court (District Court Registry Office) with confirmation of no dissolution, bankruptcy or liquidation proceedings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for Apostille member states; non-member states require consular legalization at the destination state's diplomatic mission in the Republic of Korea. No sequential combination is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing the incorporation signatories and the Korean process agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the proposed Chusik Hoesa, executed by directors whose identities and signatures are notarized by a Republic of Korea notary public or a notary public in the country where the board is convened
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for Apostille Convention jurisdictions; for non-Apostille jurisdictions, the notarized board resolution and Power of Attorney must undergo consular legalization by the destination state's consular office in Seoul without any preliminary Apostille step.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Scheduled Korean bank (banker's reference from a bank regulated by the Financial Supervisory Service and the Bank of Korea) on the applicant's existing or newly opened corporate account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank attestation plus Hague Apostille by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille member states; non-member states require consular legalization by the destination country's embassy in Seoul, applied directly to the authenticated bank letter, never following an Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate Seal Certificate (Inperk Seal Impression Certificate with notarized signature of the representative director)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean notary public and the local district court registry evidencing the seal impression filed with the corporate registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for member states; for non-members, consular legalization through the destination country's consulate or embassy in the Republic of Korea is the exclusive alternative, with no sequential chaining of Apostille and consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based enhanced due diligence requires continuous screening of each shareholder, director, president, auditor, ultimate beneficial owner, and material counterparty against the U.S. Treasury Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, and the Republic of Korea's own sanctions and financial restrictions list administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Financial Services Commission. Screenings must cover name, nationality, place of birth, residential address, identity document, and watchlists in real time, with automated alerts escalated to a designated compliance officer, false-positive investigation documented, and true matches reported as suspicious transaction reports. Politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members, and close associates must receive enhanced due diligence including source-of-wealth verification. A negative confirmation certificate is required before incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Korean Court Electronic Registration Information System (Internet Registration Office / iRO) operated by the Supreme Court of Korea
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Korean Chusik Hoesa name must be expressed in Hangul script. The statutory suffix 'Chusik Hoesa' is mandatory, and the entire official corporate name must be unique within the registration court's jurisdiction. Foreign-origin names must be phonetically transliterated into Hangul rather than translated into a semantic Korean equivalent. Four-tier naming conventions are applied: tier one is the distinctive trade mark or operator brand name; tier two is the business scope or industry identifier, for example industrial MRO or electronic catalog retail; tier three is a geographic or regional indicator if desired; and tier four is the entity-type suffix. Roman characters, Hanja characters, and Chinese characters are not permitted in the official registered corporate name, though they may appear as stylized trade names on non-statutory marketing materials only if the statutory Hangul name is also clearly displayed.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed corporate name, the applicant or its legal representative may file a written administrative appeal with the official in charge of the registration court within 30 calendar days after receipt of the written rejection. The appeal must identify the rejected name exactly, quote the statutory or jurisprudential grounds for refusal, attach a corrected name proposal or evidence of ministerial approval where a sensitive word is unavoidable, and request official reconsideration. The decision must be issued within two weeks after the appeal is complete. Simultaneously, the applicant may submit a fresh name clearance application without prejudice. If the administrative appeal is unsuccessful, a judicial appeal may be filed under the Administrative Litigation Act before the competent district court within 90 days after the appellate decision, seeking annulment of the registry's refusal and an order to accept the corrected name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address or commercial mailbox may satisfy the minimum registered-office requirement under the Commercial Act for administrative correspondence, but for this B2B industrial MRO e-commerce activity, the National Tax Service and regulated financial institutions will require a demonstrable physical business address for value added tax registration, e-tax invoice issuance, corporate bank account opening, and the place of effective management. A mere postal address is rejected as evidence of commercial substance and may expose the foreign-owned Chusik Hoesa to an official order requiring a physical office, denial of corporate banking, disqualification from public procurement, or punitive reclassification as a dormant or paper company. A serviced office with leased desk space and a visible operational presence is acceptable, provided the lease is in the company name and the company documents are physically accessible.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical on-site inspections by the National Tax Service, municipal tax authorities, or the registration court are triggered when irregularities are observed in electronic tax invoices, registered address concentration, or foreign-domestic shareholder patterns. Mandatory inspection readiness checklist: (1) signboard located at the registered office matching the registered corporate name; (2) lease or sublease agreement in the company's name covering the full inspection period; (3) at least one employee or authorized representative present during local business hours; (4) corporate books and records, including shareholder register, UBO profiles, and accounting ledgers, maintained at the registered office; (5) e-tax invoice server and terminal at the physical address; (6) evidence of MRO inventory holding or warehouse sublease exists on site or within Korea. The quantified likelihood of an unannounced inspection in the first operating year is moderate: approximately 15-20% for a low-risk standard e-commerce company, rising to 30-40% if the company claims export VAT refunds, holds a government supplier registration, or has a high ratio of non-resident shareholders.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial registration tax and local education surcharge payable to the competent district court for incorporation of a Chusik Hoesa
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean District Court Registry Office within the Ministry of Court Administration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory court filing tariff assessed on the paid-in capital floor and ordinary place of registration; non-negotiable official fee.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Issuance of Certificate of Company Registration and Corporate Seal Certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory court fee schedule for registration certificate copies and seal certificates.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the Articles of Association, Board Resolution, Power of Attorney, and corporate seal certificate by a Korean notary public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean notary public under the Notary Public Act
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Mandatory notarial schedule of the Korean Legal Profession Act; market benchmark for Korean-language notarial services ranges from 60 to 120 USD per document instrument.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille certification by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for each corporate document
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official apostille fee schedule of the Korean MOFA; per-document apostille fee approximate benchmark of 15 USD; listed amount also includes courier and administrative processing.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified English translation of the Articles of Association, Board Resolution, Power of Attorney, and compliance letters
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean licensed translation services or law firm bilingual staff
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for certified translation and proofreading of corporate legal instruments is between 100 and 200 USD per document; actual cost driven by page and complexity.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate bank account opening support, resident director appointment, and bank reference letter facilitation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Scheduled Korean bank and specialist compliance desk
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank service charges plus legal due diligence assistance based on the Korea Fair Trade Commission legal fee guideline; standard compliance retainer for bank onboarding is 350-420 USD.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due diligence, UBO piercing, PEP and sanctions screening, name clearance application, and appeal readiness

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark under the Korean Legal Profession Act rule of reasonableness; typical senior associate billing rate of 280-380 USD per hour plus junior associate rate of 120-180 USD per hour, estimated at 12 to 16 billable hours for this non-J judicial workflow.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Physical registered office preparation in a serviced office immediately available for inspection
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Serviced office operator with an address in the Seoul metropolitan or special city jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark lease rate for a 10 square meter private workspace with shared reception and mail handling is 500-700 USD per month; budget reflects first month plus security deposit amortization.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000, as amended (especially Articles 289, 295, 317, 318, 329, 383, 389, 393 and 409); the Corporate Registration Affairs Handling Rules; the Value-Added Tax Act; the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce; and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act for non-resident promoters.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Section, Civil Registry Division, Local District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the head office; online filing through the Internet Registration Office (IROS) of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea (www.iros.go.kr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company (Chusik Hoesa) under Article 317 of the Commercial Act, resulting in a Certificate of Registered Matters (corporate register extract).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None - no statutory minimum paid-up capital is required after the 2012 amendment to the Commercial Act. However, all issued shares must be fully subscribed and the full subscription price must be paid into a blocked bank deposit account in Korea, evidenced by a bank capital deposit certificate, or satisfied through court-appraised in-kind contributions, before the incorporation registration is completed. Funds are locked for restricted incorporation expenses until the company obtains its Certificate of Registered Matters.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] CHUSIK HOESA. RESOLUTION NO. 2024-01. At a duly convened first meeting of the Board of Directors of [Company Name] Chusik Hoesa, a stock corporation formed under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, held on [Date] at [Head Office Address], with all directors present and constituting a quorum, the following resolutions were adopted by unanimous vote. 1. Adoption of Share Capital and Subscription. RESOLVED, that the Company ratifies the Articles of Incorporation and the subscription schedule under which each promoter has subscribed for the number of shares set opposite his or her name, that the aggregate paid-in capital of [Won Amount] has been fully paid and deposited with [Bank] in the Republic of Korea, and that the capital deposit certificate issued by such bank is hereby accepted as evidence of payment. RESOLVED FURTHER, that any subscription representing foreign investment shall be reported to the authorities as required by the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. 2. Banking Authorization. RESOLVED, that the Company shall open, operate and maintain current, deposit, foreign currency and settlement accounts with [Bank], and that the Representative Director, together with the Chief Financial Officer, acting jointly and severally within the internal approval limits, are authorized to execute wire transfers, sign settlement instructions, open online banking sessions, accept payment cards, issue invoices, and otherwise operate the Company treasury. The bank is irrevocably authorized to act on instructions given in accordance with this resolution until written revocation is delivered. 3. Registered Office. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is established at [Full Street Address, City, Province, Republic of Korea], that this address is the legal domicile for service of process and statutory mail, and that the Representative Director is authorized to execute a lease agreement, install a corporate signboard and register the office in all applicable public records. 4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer; [Name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer; [Name] is appointed Chief Operating Officer; and [Name] is appointed Auditor, each to serve until the next general shareholders meeting and to exercise the statutory duties and powers prescribed by the Commercial Act and the Articles of Incorporation. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Representative Director is authorized to certify the Company seal, maintain the corporate seal in dual custody, and approve ordinary operating contracts, employment agreements, supplier agreements, customer catalog agreements and e-commerce marketplace agreements, subject to board approval for any transaction exceeding [Threshold]. 5. Post-Incorporation Mandates. RESOLVED, that the Representative Director is authorized to submit the incorporation registration application to the Commercial Registry, to file the business registration with the National Tax Service, to file the electronic commerce seller notification with the local municipal authority, to enroll the Company in the four major social insurance programs, to open the corporate bank accounts and to retain qualified legal counsel and external auditors. All lawful acts performed by such officers before this meeting in the Company name are ratified. 6. Effective Date. RESOLVED, that this resolution takes effect immediately and that the Company Secretary is directed to insert it in the corporate minute book and provide certified copies to banks, auditors and public authorities. Approved unanimously on [Date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Availability Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS) and the Commercial Registration Section of the Local District Court; Korean Intellectual Property Office (KIPO) for trademark check
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed Korean attorney or corporate formation agent. Log on to the Internet Registration Office (IROS) or visit the Civil Registry division of the competent Local District Court. Conduct a corporate name duplication search for the proposed English and Korean trade names against registered companies in the same jurisdiction. Run a parallel trademark search on the KIPO database for the MRO e-commerce brand. Confirm that the proposed name does not infringe the corporate name uniqueness rules of the Commercial Act as confusingly similar with an existing company. Select an available name, and where registry practice permits, reserve the name in writing. Retain the name search report, reservation receipt and payment receipts as part of the formation dossier.
required_dossiers: Proposed trade names in English and Korean transliteration
Power of attorney to formation counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is objected to as duplicative or confusingly similar, the registry will issue a correction request. File a revised name within the correction period, pay the difference in fees and re-run the search. If the objection is based on an existing trademark, obtain a coexistence consent from the senior rights holder or select an alternative brand. A formal refusal may be challenged through an administrative review before the competent court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public in the Republic of Korea, with attorneys-at-law drafting the corporate charter; final registry review later by the Local District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and finalize the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, satisfying the mandatory contents of Article 289 of the Commercial Act: business purpose, corporate name, number of authorized shares, par value, location of head office, method of public notice, and number and term of directors. For a B2B electronic catalog retailer of industrial MRO hardware, state the business purpose to include internet catalog retail of industrial maintenance parts, import and export of maintenance, repair and operations supplies, supply-chain management, e-commerce platform operations and related incidental services. Have each promoter appear before a notary public in Korea to execute a notarial deed certifying the articles and the promoters signatures. For non-resident promoters, attach apostilled or consular legalized identification and any required corporate approval from the parent entity. Ensure the notary date precedes the capital subscription payment schedule and that the articles correlate exactly with the bank subscription schedules.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in duplicate
Notarization appointment and notary fee receipt
Passport or identification of each promoter
Certificate of foreign corporate existence of non-resident promoters
Apostille or consular legalization of foreign documents
Executed embracement statements of the directors and auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or registry identifies drafting defects in the articles, execute an addendum or a new notarial deed reflecting the amendment. No substantive change after the capital payment is permitted without a new shareholders resolution. When the defect is a missing mandatory provision, amend the articles and re-notarize them within the statutory correction period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription of Shares and Blocked Capital Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank or financial institution licensed in the Republic of Korea; for foreign investment, the Foreign Exchange Bank handling the related reports
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, deposit the full subscription price for each issued share into a restricted deposit account opened in the name of the Company or its promoters at a bank located in Korea. The bank must issue a capital deposit certificate or passbook acknowledging receipt of the exact amount of paid-in capital. If the subscription is paid in cash, no withdrawal is allowed until the incorporation registration is completed, except for permitted incorporation expenses. If any shareholder contributes assets in kind, obtain an expert appraisal report from a licensed appraiser or court-appointed appraiser in accordance with the Commercial Act and list the in-kind assets in the subscription schedule. Complete shareholder subscription signatures and update the foreign investment notification if a non-resident retains shares. Maintain a complete chain-of-funds record to satisfy the bank anti-money laundering requirements.
required_dossiers: Bank capital deposit certificate or passbook
Proof of remittance or wire confirmation from each subscriber
In-kind contribution appraisal report, if applicable
Foreign investment notification acknowledgement, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the capital deposit or KYC documents, provide a declarant letter and chain-of-funds evidence, or return and re-route the remittance from the same shareholder from the same financial institution. If the deposit certificate does not match the subscriber count, open a new deposit account and abort the original capital payment. Keep the funds blocked until registration is cleared.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Section, Civil Registry Division, Local District Court; online submission through IROS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the completed Application for Registration of Incorporation with the competent Local District Court, or electronically through IROS, after the directors and auditor have accepted office. Submit the notarial deed of articles, capital deposit certificate, written consents of directors and auditor, minutes of the subscriber meeting and the first board resolution, registered office lease or title evidence, corporate seal registration form, and residence or identification copies of directors. Pay the court filing fee, registration tax and education surcharge. The court examiner performs a substantive review under Article 317 of the Commercial Act. Upon approval, obtain the Certificate of Registered Matters and the corporate seal certificate. Then immediately proceed to tax, labor and banking activation steps.
required_dossiers: Completed application for registration of incorporation
Written acceptance by directors and auditor
Registered office lease contract or proof of title
Passport/residence copies of all directors and auditor
Payment receipts for registration fee and related taxes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court examiner suspends the registration and issues a supplementary instruction, respond in writing within ten days, submit the missing certificates and pay any outstanding fee. If the application is rejected, the company may re-file or file a petition for immediate appeal under the registration appeal procedure. Legal counsel should verify the grounds to avoid repeated rejections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration, E-Commerce Seller Filing and Tax Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service through the HomeTax online portal or the local district tax office; local municipal government for electronic commerce seller notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a business registration certificate with the National Tax Service under the Value-Added Tax Act using the HomeTax online system or by visiting the responsible district tax office. Attach the certified corporate register extract, Articles of Incorporation, lease contract for the registered office, representative director identification and corporate seal certificate. File the electronic commerce seller notification under the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce with the local municipal government, disclosing the webstore domain, physical address, contact information and MRO product catalog summary. Register for VAT, corporate income tax, local income tax and e-invoice issuance obligations. If the Company uses payment gateways, complete the merchant registration under the relevant card scheme and update the B2B catalog compliance terms.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registered Matters (corporate register extract)
Lease contract for the registered office
Foreign investor accreditation certificate, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office issues a notice of error or discrepant business purpose, file an amended business registration using HomeTax. If the electronic commerce seller filing is queried, send the missing certification and revised homepage URL. Administrative appeal can be lodged with the National Tax Service Appeals Commission and subsequently with the Tax Tribunal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Activation and Mandatory Social Insurance Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank of the Companys choice; National Pension Service; National Health Insurance Service; Korea Workers Compensation and Welfare Service; local employment labor center; KOTRA Invest Korea for foreign investment reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open corporate bank accounts at the selected commercial bank in accordance with the First Board Resolution. Complete customer due diligence by submitting the certified corporate register extract, business registration certificate, board resolution, corporate seal certificate, identification of the representative director and all authorized signatories, and beneficial ownership declaration. At the same time, register the company with the National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, Korea Workers Compensation and Welfare Service and local employment center for the four major social insurance programs. If foreign investment exceeds the statutory threshold, file a foreign investment report with KOTRA Invest Korea. Confirm that all statutory officers are internally registered and that the corporate minute book contains the first board resolution and all subsequent ratification resolutions.
required_dossiers: Passport/residence identification of the representative director and signatories
Employer registration forms for social insurance
Workplace address and employee list, if any
Foreign investment report form, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account opening due to incomplete beneficial ownership information, resubmit the corrected resolution and ownership declarations. If social insurance registration misses the deadline, file an ex-post registration and pay any penalty; request an extension with the local labor authority and obtain a waiver proof if no employees exist.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable under the current digital e-commerce model - no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing operations are undertaken. The relevant non-industrial authorities are the National Tax Service for business registration and the local municipal government for the electronic commerce seller notification.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no separate industrial or manufacturing operating permit is required for ISIC 4791 electronic catalog retail of industrial maintenance hardware. The company still needs a business registration certificate and the electronic commerce seller notification, but these are not industrial operating licenses.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea, operating through the Korea Environment Corporation and delegated environmental agencies
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - ISIC 4791 internet retail does not meet the project type or size thresholds of Article 22 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act. No environmental impact assessment report or environmental registration is required for pure electronic catalog retail. If the future scope adds warehousing or distribution centers above statutory size thresholds, a new environmental screening would be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable to pure digital retail. If later warehousing or industrial activity triggers the Clean Air Conservation Act, Wastes Control Act or Water Environment Conservation Act, quantitative discharge limits, VOC emission criteria and hazardous waste handling standards would be imposed according to the facilitys capacity. If MRO supplies containing hazardous chemicals are imported or distributed, K-REACH pre-import notification, registration and chemical safety data sheet compliance would be mandatory.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For the current e-commerce back-office and order-fulfillment model, Civil Defense clearance is Not Applicable. If the company leases an office or a fulfillment warehouse, the local fire department must conduct a fire-fighting system inspection and issue a fire safety certificate for any relevant multi-use business premises under the Fire-Fighting System Installation and Maintenance Act. The employer must also complete an occupational safety and health risk assessment under the Occupational Safety and Health Act and register with the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency when employees are hired. No industrial fire permit or Civil Defense approval is required for pure digital catalog retail.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea - HomeTax electronic portal at www.hometax.go.kr; Korea Customs Service (KCS) via UNI-PASS for export trade declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the KR_CHUSIKHOESA stock corporation: (1) Register the domestic legal entity with the Korean court registry office; (2) File the Business Registration Application with the competent district tax office (or via HomeTax e-filing); (3) Attach the foreign parent company certificate of incorporation, apostilled delegation of tax representative, domestic place-of-business proof (lease or ownership), articles of incorporation, and board resolution appointing the Korean tax representative; (4) The NTS grants a 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN) used as the corporate TIN and VAT ID, evidenced by a Business Registration Certificate; (5) Activate HomeTax electronic tax invoice issuance and register the exporter with KCS UNI-PASS for customs filings. Non-resident entities without a domestic fixed place must appoint a tax representative and are not normally granted VAT registration for out-of-Korea transactions; a Korean withholding agent/reverse-charge mechanism applies instead.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea has no check-the-box election and no pass-through treatment for a Chusik Hoesa. A consolidated corporate tax election is available only for domestic wholly-owned subsidiary groups. Hybrid mismatch limitation rules apply in accordance with the Framework Act on National Taxes and OECD BEPS Action 2.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis threshold: every business operator making taxable VAT supplies must register. Small simplified taxpayer status for individuals with annual taxable turnover up to KRW 80 million, but a corporate Chusik Hoesa is subject to standard registration regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-Tax Invoice issuance for all business-to-business VAT supplies. The supplier must transmit the e-Tax Invoice to NTS HomeTax by the day after the supply; NTS operates real-time validation, cross-referencing purchase and sale ledgers. Large suppliers can integrate via NTS Open API or a licensed Value-Added Network (VAN) provider. No physical fiscal stamping is applied; anti-fraud control is performed through unique e-Tax Invoice numbers and automated mismatch detection.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from Korea to a foreign country are zero-rated under the Value-Added Tax Act where the supplier retains proof of export declaration and transportation. For B2B MRO hardware shipped from Korea, the 0% rate applies if title and risk pass to the foreign buyer, goods leave the Korean customs territory, and the exporter possesses an accepted UNI-PASS export declaration, commercial invoice, and contract. Qualifying offshore digital services and services used wholly outside Korea may likewise be zero-rated. The Korean exporter must also comply with foreign-exchange settlement requirements to evidence receipt of export proceeds, and any blocked input VAT attributable to the zero-rated export is claimable as a refund through periodic VAT returns.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) - Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS export declaration
Bill of Lading (or air waybill for air cargo) issued in the name of the Korean exporter
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Korean foreign exchange bank statement evidencing collection of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is verified ex post. Any deviation between UNI-PASS declarations, Bill of Lading data, and bank remittance records will cause NTS to disallow the 0% rate and assess the 10% VAT, plus additional tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes and, for willful evasion, criminal penalties under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. Retroactive clawback of previously credited input VAT refunds and foreign-exchange penalties under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act may apply for failure to repatriate proceeds within the statutory period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea operates a highly liberalised but administratively supervised convertible currency regime. Current account transactions such as trade in goods, service fees, royalties, and ordinary operating remittances are fully convertible without quantitative restrictions; however, each transaction must be reported and processed through a locally registered financial institution under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment (FDI) equity injections, loans, and portfolio investments, are broadly permitted for a corporation but require mandatory initial and post-investment reporting through the FEIS, an investment registration certificate for the foreign investor, and a valid taxpayer identity certificate. There is no statutory surrender or forced conversion of export proceeds, but exporters must repatriate foreign currency receivables within two years from the export declaration date unless an extension is granted by the MOEF. Profit remittances (dividends, branch earnings, or liquidation proceeds) are freely convertible after corporate income tax, with the foreign investor required to submit a withholding tax certificate, audited financial statements, and evidence of the foreign-investment registration; failure to present these documents results in administrative blocking by the domestic bank. The practical hurdles are less about currency convertibility and more about documentary precision, registration timing, and the necessity to route every cross-border transfer through a Korean Foreign Exchange Bank. Overall, the KRW is fully convertible for both current and capital purposes of a foreign-owned Chusik Hoesa, subject to a robust filing architecture rather than direct exchange controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory conversion ratio applies to export proceeds; the statutory requirement is repatriation, not surrender. Exporters must collect and repatriate foreign exchange earned from exports within two years from the date of the export declaration (extendable to five years for vessel or equipment exports with MOEF approval). The exporter may retain 100% of the foreign currency in a domestic foreign-currency deposit account or convert it to KRW at the market rate through an authorised Foreign Exchange Bank, but every receipt must be reported to the FEIS within 30 days of receipt.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Investment) and Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW/FCY)
Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Investment) and Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Investment) and Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Investment) and Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for pure offshore digital EMI platforms (e.g., Wise, Revolut, or unlicensed global payment wallets). Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, only licensed foreign exchange business institutions (Korean banks with global business licences or Money Exchange Business registrees) can operate an FEIS-reportable account for a Korean resident entity. Offshore EMIs cannot provide KRW IBAN/account numbers, cannot issue statutory Korean bank statements for customs or capital verification, and cannot serve as an account designated for the foreign-investment registration process. Such EMIs may act only as a supplementary payment execution node for outbound GBP/USD payments if the primary settlement account remains at a domestic Tier-1 bank. For a Chusik Hoesa requiring orderly FDI registration and capital verification, all inward capital injections must clear through a registered Korean foreign-exchange bank; an offshore EMI would trigger reporting failure and potential penalty if used for capital subscription.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean commercial banks generally require at least one statutory director (or a corporate secretary with a registered power of attorney) to appear physically in-branch for first-time KYC confirmation and issuance of the Foreign Investment Registration approval. Some Tier-1 banks permit a consular-remote opening protocol: the director signs the account application in front of a Korean consulate officer or a notary public in the domicile jurisdiction, followed by apostilled corporate documents and a video interview with the bank's compliance team. A fully remote proxy opening without any physical attendance is rarely permitted for a foreign-invested entity, because the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act mandates the bank to verify the identity of the ultimate beneficial owner and the actual representative of the FDI. The recommended standard is: statutory representative (or a sole director) physically in Seoul for an initial branch visit; subsequent account operations may be delegated to a CFO under a formal internal resolution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from a jurisdiction with high financial secrecy or unexplained personal wealth of the UBO
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Audited financial statements of the sole shareholder for the last three years; (2) tax returns and tax payment receipts in the shareholder's domicile; (3) bank reference letter from the remitting financial institution highlighting the account history; (4) certified source-of-wealth statement and employment/business income records; (5) notarised undertaking that funds originate from lawful commercial activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared B2B MRO commerce and high-frequency small-value wire settlements inconsistent with industrial procurement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Master supply contract with ISO Incoterms and delivery schedules; (2) purchase orders and corresponding commercial invoices for each transaction batch; (3) warehouse logistics documentation, bill of lading, or parcel tracking records; (4) internal ERP report showing the vendor onboarding process and product catalogues; (5) annual sales forecast explaining the transaction cadence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner or counterparty appears in a sanctions list or a high-risk-country PEP database
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Independent screening results from a licensed EDD provider; (2) detailed relationship disclosure and rationale for the business connection; (3) certification of no Syrian/North Macedonian/Iranian/Russian-affiliated connections; (4) board resolution approving the risk acceptance; (5) consent to ongoing transaction monitoring and an undertaking to provide additional source-of-funds documentation on demand.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border card-brand settlement (Credit Card rails) used as a primary mechanism for B2B industrial MRO invoices, triggering unverifiable payment flow
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Merchant Contact Point and card-acquiring agreement with a Korean PG (payment gateway) company; (2) monthly reconciliation between card settlements and delivered MRO products; (3) customer credit policy and refund controls; (4) a detailed explanation of why card rails are used rather than bank transfer; (5) external audit trail of card chargebacks and settlement claims.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inward FDI capital must be remitted via SWIFT MT103 from the foreign shareholder's bank to the Korean escrow bank designated in the Foreign Investment Registration Report. The remittance must carry a clear beneficiary name matching the Korean entity, a purpose of payment code under the Bank of Korea classification (usually 'FDIX' or '133010' for equity investment), and must be accompanied by a copy of the Foreign Investment Registration Certificate (or report number) sent via SWIFT field 70/72. The receiving Canadian domestic bank will provisionally credit the capital escrow account, verify the foreign exchange declaration in the FEIS, and then issue a Certificate of Capital Introduction ('Foreign Capital Import') which is essential for annual customs verification and tax clearance. The company must then have the bank complete a 'Settlement of Foreign Exchange' report within 30 days and transfer the funds into an operational KRW account after exercising the currency conversion. Funds must not be fragmented across multiple accounts; a single designated escrow account should be used to maintain a clean audit trail.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For payment of industrial MRO inventory to international suppliers, the preferred clearing rail is an SWIFT MT103 documentary cheque for amounts under USD 200,000, with a commercial invoice and purchase order attached to the bank remitting. For higher-value or structured shipments, a Uniform Rules for Demand Guarantee (URDG) backed Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700 issue / MT754 advice) is advisable, with a beneficiary bank at the supplier's side receiving a presentation of transport documents, packing lists, and insurance certificates. Documentary Collections (URC 522, DP/DA) remain permissible but require a formal collection instruction to the supplier's bank; these carry higher counterparty risk and are used only for trust-tested suppliers. All outbound payments must be submitted with a 'Foreign Exchange Business Reporting' form, quoting the corresponding purpose code linked to the trade (e.g., 'Measurement & Control devices under ISIC 4791 MRO'), and the bank will file the FEIS transaction report. Payments for intangible services or royalties require a separate withholding tax certificate to be deposited with the bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore FX forward contracts (maturity up to 12 months) with Korean foreign-exchange banks, restricted to trade documented by import/export contracts
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) on foreign-currency-denominated loans and bonds issued by the Korean corporation

Korean won non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are generally prohibited for onshore residents; however, offshore NDFs may be used only for certain non-liberalised currency pairs and require MOEF approval – not recommended for standard MRO trade hedging
Flexible FX options (call/put) with forward delivery optionality, permitted only if the bank confirms an underlying current or capital-account exposure
Plain currency swaps for financing purposes where both principal and interest remittances are tied to a real commercial contract

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Attached Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via Hometax Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 of the calendar year immediately following a December 31 fiscal year-end; for a non-calendar fiscal year, within three months after the end of that fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid corporate income tax (40% for transactions with tax-haven related parties), underreporting penalty of 10% of the underreported amount (40% for fraudulent underreporting), delinquency charge of 0.022% per day computed on unpaid principal (approximately 8.03% per annum), asset seizure under tax disposition, and repeated non-compliance leading to court-ordered dissolution and strike-off from the Korean corporate registry

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surtax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the national corporate income tax return: by March 31 for December 31 fiscal year-end, or within three months after the end of the fiscal year for a non-calendar fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional local tax penalty of up to 20% of unpaid local corporate income tax, local tax delinquency charge of 0.022% per day on unpaid amounts, demands on the registered office, seizure of corporate bank accounts and assets, and referral for registration cancellation after prolonged non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting Approval of Financial Statements and Statutory Minute Book and Registers Maintenance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records at registered office; changes to directors or representative directors filed with the district court having jurisdiction over the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual general meeting must be convened within three months after the end of each fiscal year under the Korean Commercial Act; director and representative director registration changes must be filed within two weeks after the AGM resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may be subject to administrative fines of up to KRW 5,000,000 for failing to hold or approve the AGM agenda without just cause; late court registration of director changes may trigger per-day overdue registration fines, adverse third-party protection loss, and administrative correction orders ultimately supporting dissolution proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Auditor's Report Filing and DART Submission (Only Where Mandatory Audit Threshold Is Met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART electronic disclosure system, with the audit report also attached to the NTS corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit report must be finalized and presented to the annual general meeting, and filed through DART where applicable, no later than the statutory AGM deadline for the relevant fiscal year (March 31 for December 31 fiscal year-end); if FSS prescribes a different DART docket date, the earlier date governs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint a registered external auditor, failure to obtain an independent CPA audit report, or failure to file the auditor's report through DART subjects the corporation to administrative fines under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, FSS ability to force designation of an auditor at corporate expense, possible invalidity of financial statements for tax and dividend purposes, referral to the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants for discipline, and repeated violations leading to prosecution and deregistration

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, an independent certified CPA audit is mandatory for a Chusik Hoesa where: (1) total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year are at least KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9,100,000); (2) the company is listed on KOSPI/KOSDAQ, is a bank, insurance company, securities company, financial holding company, or other financial institution designated by law; (3) the company is designated as a public-interest company or is required by the Financial Services Commission due to material accounting risks; or (4) the company falls within prescribed Presidential Decree criteria, including total assets of at least KRW 7,000,000,000 (approximately USD 5,300,000) combined with financial distress triggers such as 50% or more capital erosion, three consecutive years of operating losses, or failure to correct accounting irregularities. Additionally, lenders, shareholders holding 3% or more of voting shares, or board resolutions may require an audit under the Commercial Act even when the statutory test is not met.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) as aligned with IFRS is compulsory for audit-mandatory stock corporations; a non-audit-trigger Chikusa Hoesa may prepare financial statements using Korean GAAP for non-public entities (K-GAAP SME standards) unless the tax law or a creditor agreement requires K-IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not maintain a general-purpose annual beneficial ownership register for ordinary private Chusik Hoesa companies. Under the Commercial Act, a shareholder register showing each member's name, address, share class, share count, and payment detail must be kept at the registered office, and any transfer of shares must be reflected in that register as of the effective date. Director and representative director changes must be filed with the competent district court registry within two weeks of the legal event. If a foreign investor acquires or disposes of an interest in a Korean corporation, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act requires post-reporting to the Ministry of Economy and Finance through KOTRA or a designated foreign exchange bank within 30 days after the underlying change, though this is event-driven rather than an annual confirmation. Financial institutions also require UBO identification and annual AML/KYC customer risk review at the banking relationship level, but this is not a government registry filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Statutory Auditor or Audit Committee Minutes
Minute Book of General Shareholder Meetings and Board of Directors Meetings
Corporate Articles of Incorporation and Ordinary Resolutions Archive

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 to USD 1,500 per year for a standard registered office or corporate service agent in Seoul/Gyeonggi province, including statutory mail handling, court correspondence, and tax notification reception
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 to USD 20,000 per year for a typical non-listed Chusik Hoesa, increasing with total assets, transaction volume, group consolidation scope, and whether an FSS-designated audit firm is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top marginal rate; progressive brackets apply: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200,000,000; 19% on KRW 200,000,001 to KRW 20,000,000,000; 21% on KRW 20,000,000,001 to KRW 300,000,000,000; 24% above KRW 300,000,000,000.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign-invested high-technology enterprises in Free Economic Zones may receive a 100% corporate tax holiday for 5 years and a 50% exemption for the following 2 years. SMEs and qualifying entities may benefit from reduced effective tax rates through R&D tax credits, facility investment credits, job creation credits, and enhanced deductions for qualifying industrial innovation expenses.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 1, with attached schedules for taxable income computation, loss carryforward, tax credits, and transfer pricing disclosures) filed electronically via HomeTax (hometax.go.kr).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; a first-half interim corporate tax prepayment is required for corporations with prior-year tax liabilities above the statutory threshold.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate tax return must be filed within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., March 31 for a December 31 year-end). Interim prepayment for the first six months is due within 2 months after the interim period (e.g., August 31 for a calendar-year corporation).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal taxpayer identification number assigned by the district tax office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident foreign corporations with a domestic place of business must enter the registration number issued to that Korean permanent establishment, not the home country registration number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered Korean legal name of the Chusik Hoesa and the name of its statutory representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean branch name and the domestic place of business manager; if the head office is foreign, attach a certified copy of the head office registration and proof of appointment of the Korean branch representative.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Fiscal Year and Settlement Date
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The taxable period reported, from the first day to the last day of the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The domestic place of business must close its books as of the same fiscal year end as the head office, unless a different fiscal year is approved by the National Tax Service.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross receipts from B2B MRO electronic catalog sales, including credit card sales and SWIFT wire settlement receipts, before deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Korean-source gross sales attributable to the domestic place of business; trading with non-Korean related parties must be included and referenced on the transfer pricing schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 10a - Operating Expenses and Deductible Costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total ordinary and necessary business expenses attributable to earning the Korean-source income, including cost of goods sold, logistics, platform, and overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses directly allocated to the domestic place of business are deductible; head-office overhead allocations must be supported by contemporaneous documentation and remain within arm's length limits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 19a - Taxable Income Before Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed basis after applying accounting-to-tax adjustments, excluding carryforward losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations should ensure that transfer pricing adjustments and thin capitalization limits are reflected; income allocation to the domestic permanent establishment must follow the OECD attributable profit method.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permitted deduction for eligible net operating losses carried forward within the statutory 5-year period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign corporation's domestic permanent establishment may deduct approved prior losses only to the extent they are attributable to Korean-source business and have been duly reported.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computed by applying the progressive corporate income tax rates to the final tax base after all adjustments and loss offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the same progressive rate schedule as resident corporations; no separate non-resident corporate rate exists for a taxable domestic permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 50a - Tax Credits and Special Deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for R&D, facility investment, job creation, foreign tax credits, and tax treaty reductions claimed on the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident may claim treaty-based withholding reductions by attaching the approved Application for Tax Treaty Exemption/Reduction and the certificate of residence; otherwise the statutory withholding was already imposed at source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 60a - Total Tax Payable and Prepayments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate tax liability after deducting interim prepayments, withheld taxes, and prior installments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any excess interim prepayment or foreign withholding credit may be refunded after filing; contracts and payment rail records must be retained to substantiate the prepayments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the corporate income tax return attracts a surtax of 20% of the unpaid tax. Understated tax from negligent omission is subject to a 10% penalty, while fraudulent or unjust omission attracts a 30%-40% penalty. Late payment incurs daily interest at the statutory rate, currently 0.022% per day (approximately 8.03% per annum), plus additional administrative fines. Failure to attach mandatory transfer pricing documentation may result in separate fines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national withholding tax plus a 10% local income tax surcharge on the national tax (2% effective), resulting in a total statutory dividend withholding rate of 22% on gross distributions to non-resident corporate shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced rate under an applicable double tax treaty, the non-resident payee must submit, through the payer or directly to the Korean source tax office, the Application for Withholding Tax Exemption/Reduction under Tax Treaty together with a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the competent tax authority of the residence state. The TRC must evidence the beneficial owner status, and where required, ownership and holding period requirements (typically 6 months or more for treaty dividend benefits). The application should be made before the income is remitted or before the withholding tax return due date. After filing, the payer may apply the treaty rate on subsequent remittances; refunds are available if statutory withholding was applied pending approval.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and interest paid to non-residents are each subject to 20% national withholding plus 2% local income tax surcharge, totaling 22% in the absence of treaty relief. Under most Korean double tax treaties, interest rates are commonly reduced to 10%-15%, and royalties to 5%-10%, depending on the counterparty state and the nature of the IP. The beneficial owner must satisfy the treaty limitation-on-benefits / principal-purpose test to secure the reduced rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion aggregate foreign related-party transactions triggers mandatory preparation of a Local File and Master File. A transfer pricing disclosure summary must accompany the corporate tax return when cross-border related-party transactions reach KRW 5 billion. A Country-by-Country Report is due for multinational groups with consolidated group revenue exceeding KRW 1 trillion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not maintain a standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime, but economic substance is effectively enforced through the Corporate Tax Act General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR), the International Tax Coordination Act CFC rules, and treaty anti-abuse doctrines including the Principal Purpose Test and beneficial ownership requirements. A Chusik Hoesa lacking local employees, offices, board activity, and substantive operational control cannot rely on paper presence; transactions may be recharacterized, treaty benefits denied, and deductions disallowed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully omitting B2B e-commerce revenue from electronic catalog sales, fabricating deductible expenses, suppressing SWIFT wire receivables or credit card settlement records, and submitting knowingly false corporate income or VAT returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine of up to KRW 50 million is imposed for fraudulent evasion; in aggravated or repeated cases the penalty increases to up to 10 years' imprisonment and a fine not exceeding KRW 100 million, in addition to full tax assessment, surcharges, and 40% unjust-evasion penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who participate in, direct, or knowingly benefit from tax evasion are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax and penalties. Courts may pierce the corporate veil, order civil restitution, impose immediate departure bans, freeze personal bank accounts, and imprison responsible directors upon conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Korean Chusik Hoesa without meaningful local staff, physical premises, inventory, or business judgment while using the entity solely to invoice MRO supplies, obtain treaty benefits, or shift profits within a multinational group.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service may invoke the GAAR to recharacterize the transactions, deny expense deductions, impose a 40% penalty on unjust underpricing, deny foreign tax credits, and revoke treaty shelter benefits. Corporate registration itself may be administratively closed for chronically failing to satisfy the substantial business purpose test.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally assessed for the resulting unpaid corporate tax and withholding obligations as management officers responsible for compliance. Asset preservation orders, travel restrictions, and criminal liability for aiding profit-shifting are applied where the shell arrangement is used for intentional tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's length management fees, royalties, interest, or product margins to foreign related parties; failing to create or submit the Master File, Local File, or CbC Report; or failing to apply an approved TP method with proper benchmarking.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may make a transfer pricing adjustment recalculating Korean-source taxable income, add unpaid corporate income tax plus daily late-payment interest of 0.022%, impose an understatement penalty of up to 30% or 40% for unjust deficiency, and levy an administrative fine of up to KRW 30 million for missing or late TP documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who certified inaccurate TP records or who knowingly approved profit-stripping transactions are individually liable for the resultant tax deficit to the extent of their fault, may be subject to civil restitution claims by creditors or minority shareholders, and may face travel bans while under investigation, plus imprisonment in fraud-aggravated cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering / Abusive Payment Rail Use
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the B2B e-commerce vehicle to process credit card or SWIFT wire payments for third parties, issuing invoices for transactions without underlying goods, or failing to disclose suspicious cross-border transactions to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Financial Transactions Reports Act imposes administrative fines up to KRW 50 million for AML compliance failures and KRW 100 million for missing suspicious transaction reports. Unlicensed foreign exchange business under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act carries imprisonment of up to 3 years or a fine of up to KRW 30 million, plus possible confiscation of transaction proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who allow the corporate treasury to be used for third-party money transmission can be held criminally liable for aiding unlicensed remittance and money laundering; they face personal disgorgement, civil liability to defrauded counterparties, travel bans, and imprisonment in aggravated money laundering conspiracies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to withhold the statutory 22% (or applicable treaty-reduced) tax on dividend, royalty, or interest remittances to non-residents; paying distributions without filing the withholding return; or claiming treaty relief without an approved certificate of residence and beneficial ownership proof.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service assesses the entire unreported withholding tax on the gross remittance, adds a 20% non-withholding penalty or a 10% underreporting penalty, and charges daily late-payment interest. Criminal fines apply for intentional failure to withhold where the amount exceeds the criminal threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the payment of withheld taxes that were lawfully collected but not remitted to the Treasury. Repeated violations can trigger piercing of the corporate veil, civil restitution orders, travel bans, and imprisonment of the responsible officers under the Joint Penal Provisions of the Framework Act on National Taxes.
